# Fig 2 — `final_benchmark` caption (generated by `scripts/manuscript_figures/final_benchmark.py`)

Fig 2 | Trustworthy PAS detection: the final Stage-2 run (PeakATail code 9dfdefb, #96 + #97 merged) against the competitor panel. Definitions: atlas-agreement precision = fraction of calls within 100 bp (point, strand-matched) of a PolyASite 2.0 representative site; it is agreement with a curated atlas, not ground truth (atlas-novel true sites count as false positives). R_det denominator = atlas sites in genes detected in the dataset (285,136 human / 126,686 mouse); full-atlas recall of the default 0.089 (PBMC; 569,005) and 0.098 / 0.100 (mice; 301,006). One scorer (score_tool.py), same denominators for every tool; 3-seed gene-body-shuffled nulls. scUTRquant is catalog-based (hollow, not ranked). Pre-registration: the precision-first default and its P@100 ≥ 0.50 gate were committed before the ORIGINAL run and are unchanged here (gate 01:19, original arms 02:59, v2 re-run 16:14, all 2026-08-21; 13 §1, 19); the ≥2-molecule threshold was pre-registered before that run (12 CORRECTION). Gate: PASS on all three (0.706 / 0.745 / 0.757); no ≥1-molecule output clears the original P ≥ 0.38 floor. The v1 run (code 4efeb125, 15) gave 0.717 / 0.741 / 0.755; the −1.1 pp PBMC move is the corrected minus-strand IP window (#96), reconstructed key-for-key. The IP filter buys +5.3 pp atlas-agreement precision for −1.2 pp R_det (mouse 1); compute 12.5 GB / ~28-35 min on PBMC (was 294 GB / 3:46 h); 19 §1/§3. Caveats: single PBMC donor / BAM; the two mice are one study and chemistry; the default's recall is at or below polyApipe's (-12% PBMC, -18% mouse) and the F1_det lead (+0.020 / +0.014) is not a meaningful margin — the claim is precision, not overall accuracy. The non-IP PBMC ≥2-molecule file (pas_tier1_ge2mol_noIP_POSTHOC) is not the default and is not shown. Verified: final_v2_verify/VERIFIED_v2.md (FIXED). Every plotted value: results/figures/manuscript/final_benchmark*.tsv.

**Panel a** — PBMC 10k v3: atlas-agreement precision @100 bp (y) vs detected-gene recall R_det @100 bp (x) for
every tool; PeakATail as a connected path of operating points (shipped → both tiers, no IP → tier-1 ≥1 mol, no IP
→ tier-1 ≥1 mol, IP → precision default = tier-1 ∩ IP-pass ∩ ≥2 distinct clip molecules). Light-grey F1_det
isolines 0.1–0.4; dashed line = pre-registered gate P ≥ 0.50 (13 §1); dotted line + dotted isoline = original
two-sided gate P ≥ 0.38 & F1_det > 0.261 (10 §5). Small ticks at the bottom = mean of the 3-seed gene-body-shuffled
null for each call set. scTail is absent: not runnable on this BAM (R1 = 28 bp).
**Panel b** — GSE104556 testis, two mice as mean ± range (both mice in the TSV); all mouse arms ran with the IP
filter so the path has no "no IP" step; SCAPTURE is mouse 1 only. **Panel c** — n sites scored per call set, log
scale. **Panel d** — PeakATail tier decomposition on the PBMC IP arm: tier-2 / tier-1 single-molecule / tier-1 ≥2
molecules (= default), with the atlas-agreement precision @100 bp of each scored output (tier-2 0.056,
tier-1 ≥1 mol 0.352, default 0.706); 72.2% of tier-1 sites are single-molecule
(121,041 / 167,565; mouse 50.3% / 48.8%).
Definition matters here: this ratio is 1 − n(default) / n(tier-1) **on the IP arm shown here**; the same ratio on the no-IP arm is 72.1% (1 − 62,110 / 222,955) — the verifier's recount and the value the manuscript text quotes (19 §4), superseding 15 §4's 72.5% (the v1 IP arm).
